metadata.case_name: POON CHI SANG LOUIS v. J.V. FITNESS LTD T/A CALIFORNIA FITNESS

plaintiff.occupation_before: sergeant of the Hong Kong Police Force (the Force). He worked in the Emergency Unit performing frontline duties on shift
plaintiff.occupation_after: instructor at the Police College (performing demonstrations and giving instructions, with assistant helping him on physical trainings; regular hours Mon to Fri and not on shifts)

injuries.description: soft tissue wound laceration over the anterior and distal aspect of plaintiff's right leg
source: Dr. Miu diagnosed that the Accident resulted in soft tissue wound laceration as well as contusion injury over the anterior and distal aspect of plaintiff’s right leg.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of lower leg

injuries.description: contusion injury over the anterior and distal aspect of plaintiff's right leg
source: Dr. Miu diagnosed that the Accident resulted in soft tissue wound laceration as well as contusion injury over the anterior and distal aspect of plaintiff’s right leg.
injuries.icd_description: Contusion of other or unspecified parts of lower leg

manifestations.description: feeling stiff and numb at times
healed scar over its anterior surface running obliquely and measuring 8 cm, with slight increase in pigmentation but not hypertrophic and mild swelling around it
reduced exercise tolerance / current exercise performance and tolerance has been impaired

source: He received suturing (7 stitches) under local anesthesia and wound dressing in the out-patient department.
He received suturing (7 stitches) under local anesthesia and wound dressing in the out-patient department.

treatments_received.treatment: first dose of tetanus vaccine (and subsequent second and third doses)
source: First dose of tetanus vaccine was administered to him.
He attended STH again on 19 Sept 2015. ... Second dose of tetanus vaccine was administered
About 6 months later, the plaintiff received his third dose of tetanus vaccine.

treatments_received.treatment: silicone gel sheet for scar reduction
source: He attended STH again on 19 Sept 2015. ... silicone gel sheet was given to him for scar reduction.
He was discharged home with oral medication.

treatments_received.treatment: consultations with traditional Chinese medicine practitioners, acupuncturists and physiotherapists (irregular basis)
source: he now consults traditional Chinese medicine practitioners, acupuncturists and physiotherapists for symptomatic treatment of his wound on an irregular basis.

treatments_future.treatment: symptomatic treatment (medication and physiotherapy) on a need-to basis
source: The prognosis, opined Dr Miu, would likely be satisfactory only. The right leg pain the plaintiff still suffers would most likely persist, with episodes of exacerbation of right leg pain after exertion, marching or prolonged work. He would require symptomatic treatment (in the form of medication and physiotherapy) on a need-to basis.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: As a result of the Accident ... the plaintiff had once stopped sports activities altogether, had later reduced his sport activities for some time, and had ceased bicycle training altogether for some time; current exercise performance and tolerance of the plaintiff has been impaired, due to intermittent exacerbation of pain caused by the Accident; his plan of getting trained as a part-time coach of fitness bicycle has been deferred as a result of the Accident.
He often engages in sports together with his wife and enjoys much doing so ... he regretted much for letting down his wife in these periods.

comparable_cases.case_name: Lee Yau Wai v. Yeung Kam Wing
comparable_cases.injury_description: Involved several surgical procedures for right wrist and left knee, including wrist arthroscopy, reconstruction of ligament, debridement and left knee operation; victim gave up various vigorous sports.

comparable_cases.case_name: Poon Man Chun v. Li Sau Yee
comparable_cases.injury_description: Large open wound over right knee and leg area; operated on with fractured knee-cap fixed with screws; several more operations followed; later transfer from job; walked with slight limp and left with unsightly knee scars; could no longer swim certain strokes and had to give up other sports.

comparable_cases.case_name: Ng Ka Ho (an infant) v Yeung Kwok Leung
comparable_cases.injury_description: Head injuries without loss of consciousness, minor right knee injuries without fracture treated with suturing and discharged same day; dizziness and vomiting subsided spontaneously; mild post-traumatic distress symptoms and aggravation of pervasive developmental disorder.

comparable_cases.case_name: Wong Ming Kwan v. Wing Ming Electrical Company Limited and others
comparable_cases.injury_description: Right leg severely cut causing multiple lacerations with tendon exposed; complete cut of right anterior tibial artery, deep peroneal nerve and several tendons; operation to repair artery, nerve and tendons; post-op brace and crutches; intensive physiotherapy and further supports; over 2 years sick leave and residual pain, stiffness and numbness.

comparable_cases.case_name: Mahmood Tariq v Kinway Engineering Ltd & Anor
comparable_cases.injury_description: Victim fell from height; had back sprain and right knee contusion; discharged after 2 days; analgesics and 15 sessions of physiotherapy; over 12 months total sick leave; later local tenderness and reduced lumbar spine movement noted.

comparable_cases.case_name: Chung Wai Hung v Chung Wai Ming
comparable_cases.injury_description: 7-cm cut wound over left anterior knee, deep to proximal tibia with tear of patella tendon and contamination; operation with debridement and tendon repair; knee brace post-op; persistent left knee pain, slight limp, inability to run or squat, pain on stair negotiation; left with 6-cm scar.
